references.text: Solomon mentions the covenant the Lord made with the Israelites when He brought them out of Egypt, a direct parallel to Deuteronomy's description of the covenant with the fathers.
Jeremiah describes exactly the same reason for punishment: they abandoned the Lord's covenant and worshiped other gods, using the same expression about the exodus from Egypt.
The basis for the covenant made at Sinai, where Israel was to be God's treasured possession if they kept the covenant.
Moses makes the covenant with the people on the Lord's behalf, the same covenant referred to in Deuteronomy 29:24.
A warning against forgetting the Lord's covenant and making an idol, with the same link between breaking the covenant and apostasy.
The prophecy that the people will break the covenant and abandon God, which corresponds to the explanation of punishment in 29:24.
Israel rejected the Lord's covenant and followed idols, leading to exile - a fulfillment of the warning in Deuteronomy.
The angel of the Lord reminds them of the covenant and the exodus from Egypt, and warns against breaking the covenant.
